title: Cells with Odd Values in a Matrix
statement:
Start from an `m x n` grid filled with zeros. Each entry `indices[i] = [ri, ci]` (0-indexed) triggers two steps: add 1 to every cell of row `ri`, then add 1 to every cell of column `ci` (so the cell `(ri, ci)` gains 2).

After processing every entry of `indices`, return how many cells of the grid hold an odd number.
signature: int oddCells(int m, int n, int[][] indices)
notes:
## Intuition

The direct simulation builds the whole matrix and, for every entry of `indices`, adds 1 along a row and a column: O(k · (m + n)) work plus O(m · n) memory. But a cell's final value is just *(times its row was chosen) + (times its column was chosen)*. So simulate the operations on two small counter arrays instead of the grid, then read each cell's value from its row and column counters.

## Approach

1. Make `rows` (length `m`) and `cols` (length `n`), all zero.
2. For each `[r, c]` in `indices`, add 1 to `rows[r]` and to `cols[c]`.
3. Walk over every cell `(i, j)`; its value is `rows[i] + cols[j]`. Count it when that sum is odd.
4. Return `count`.

## Example 1, step by step

`m = 2`, `n = 3`, `indices = [[0,1],[1,1]]`. After the loop, `rows = [1, 1]` and `cols = [0, 2, 0]`. Row 0 holds `1 + 0, 1 + 2, 1 + 0 = 1, 3, 1`, all odd; row 1 is the same. So `count = 6`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(k + m · n) for the k operations and the scan of the grid.
- Space: O(m + n) for the two counter arrays.

## Pitfalls

- The cell `(ri, ci)` gains 2, not 1; working with counters handles this automatically.
- Only parity matters, so the follow-up's O(m + n) answer is `oddRows · (n - oddCols) + (m - oddRows) · oddCols`: a cell is odd when exactly one of its row and column was chosen an odd number of times.
- The same pair can appear several times; each occurrence counts.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `rows[i]` | how many operations touched row `i` |
| `cols[j]` | how many operations touched column `j` |
| `r`, `c` | the row and column of the current operation |
| `count` | number of odd cells found so far |

narration.2: rows[i] counts how many operations add 1 to row i.
narration.3: cols[j] counts how many operations add 1 to column j.
narration.5: Replay every operation on the counters instead of on the full grid.
narration.6: This operation adds 1 to each cell of row r.
narration.7: It also adds 1 to each cell of column c.
narration.11: Visit every row of the final grid...
narration.12: ...and every column, so each cell is checked once.
narration.13: A cell's value is its row count plus its column count; check whether it is odd.
narration.18: Return the number of odd cells.
